newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to set up new fair trading watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to set up new fair trading watchdog.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to merge the Fair Trading Commission and Department of Internal Trade to protect consumer interests and fight anti-competitive practices, government officials said on Wednesday.

"The aim is to fall in line with the emerging free market environment and to prevent overlapping," a Trade Ministry official said. "Other countries like the U.K. and Australia have only one authority for fair trade and consumer protection."
A key feature of the planned merger and reform of the consumer protection laws would be the setting up of a tribunal to adjudicate where offences had been committed without going to court, he said.
"We're drafting new laws to take care of threats to fair trade arising out of new situations like the privatisation of state enterprises, such as monopolies," he said.
"It is our responsibilty to ensure that the process does not work against the public interest," he added.
A Fair Trading Commission official said the organisation had the power to monitor price hikes and recommend changes if they were seen to be unfair and went against consumer interests.
The government is embroiled in a dispute with the gas monopoly, Shell Gas Lanka, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, after it raised prices twice in one year.
The company, formerly the state gas monopoly, was restricted to prices hikes of 10 percent a year under the privatisation agreement.
The government has said it is trying to renegotiate the deal with Shell.
Shell acquired a 51 percent stake in the firm for $37 million in 1995.
